issues: Whether a folding knife whose blade deploys rapidly and locks open via a flipper tab, and whose deployment cannot be slowed or stopped once initiated, falls within the definition of a prohibited weapon under s. 2(3) of the Criminal Code (knife that opens by force of gravity or by centrifugal force)
Whether a prohibited weapon as defined in the Criminal Code is a prohibited import under the Customs Act, and whether the CBSA is thereby required to refuse entry
Whether the fact that identical or substantially similar knives are openly sold in Canadian retail stores constitutes a valid ground to set aside a CBSA refusal of entry for a prohibited import
Whether the stated purpose of importation (personal use or gift, not resale) is a relevant factor or available defence to the importation of a prohibited weapon
Whether the absence of criminal enforcement (no charges for sale or possession of similar knives) is a relevant consideration in an administrative decision to refuse entry of a prohibited import
The standard of review applicable to a CBSA decision classifying imported goods as prohibited weapons and refusing entry
The proper procedural avenue and applicable standard for challenging a CBSA importation refusal after internal reconsideration has been exhausted
key_facts: Approximately ten inexpensive folding knives ordered from an overseas seller and shipped by mail
Each knife has a flipper tab near the pivot; pressing it with one finger causes the blade to swing out rapidly and lock fully open
Once blade deployment begins, it cannot be slowed or stopped
Knives were held and refused entry by CBSA as prohibited weapons
CBSA confirmed the refusal on reconsideration
Client asserts identical or nearly identical knives are sold in Canadian outdoor and sporting goods retail chains
Client asserts the knives were purchased as a holiday gift, not for resale
Client asserts no one has been criminally charged in Canada for selling or carrying such knives
causes_of_action: Judicial review of CBSA importation refusal decision
candidate_statutes: Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, s. 2(3) (definition of prohibited weapon — knife opening by force of gravity or centrifugal force)
Customs Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-49, s. 34 (prohibited imports)
Customs Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-49, s. 100 (seizure and detention of prohibited goods)
